owner_decisions: The primary fixture uses an explicit five-chaos base and Restart price; this is a fixture input, not a universal default.
All four goal slots require the named naturally rolled T1 modifier families; crafted or unveiled relatives do not satisfy them.

The solve uses Calculator goal-relevant action discovery and goal-progress-gated destructive reforges, excludes optional economic Restart, and retains mechanic-owned replacement recovery such as a failed Fracture attempt.

The automatic Eldritch Exalt case keeps the primitive dependency-only and requires its carrier-local prefix retry option to retain an already satisfied fractured suffix goal on every continuation; its disclosed 0.001-chaos Eldritch Exalt and paired 0.001-chaos Eldritch Annul cleanup overrides against the pinned 3.59- and 40.53-chaos snapshot quotes are synthetic bounded-retry forced-winner inputs, not a live-optimality claim.

The Influence Exalt case uses a Warlord-only natural family goal on an uninfluenced Vaal Regalia, so the canonical market-priced Warlord Exalt must be retained and selected through the ordinary product path without a forced action-price override.

The Imprint case freezes the dynamic public-product gate's lowest-weight natural prefix and highest-weight compatible natural suffix, retains the quoted Craicic Croaker and owner-default rare-beast prices, and discloses only the two non-Bestiary retry-route overrides already qualified by that gate.
Every relevant family must complete, prove non-improving, win, or report a deterministic rejection; a cap-stopped Chaos policy is not exact.
The case succeeds only with exact lower/upper equality and an independently evaluated compiled policy within five minutes.
